# Lab 1:
For this lab, we will be using some basic data manipulation and plotting commands in R.  We are working with a data set that is comparing the transcript profiles from peripheral B lymphocytes between patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and normal healthy controls.  The GEO summary of the data set is as follows: 

Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease with an important clinical and biological heterogeneity. B lymphocytes appear central to the development of SLE which is characterized by the production of a large variety of autoantibodies and hypergammaglobulinemia. In mice, immature B cells from spontaneous lupus prone animals are able to produce autoantibodies when transferred into immunodeficient mice, strongly suggesting the existence of intrinsic B cell defects during lupus. In order to approach these defects in humans, we compared the peripheral B cell transcriptomes of quiescent lupus patients to normal B cell transcriptomes.  

## Q1) Data Setup and Loading appropriate libraries
```{r}
#| label: setup
# Load core library for visualization
library(ggplot2)
```

## Q2) Unzip the text file, and read into R 
```{r}
data <- read.table("sle_b_cell.txt", 
                  header = TRUE, 
                  row.names = 1)

# Extract the first row
head(data, 1)

```
## Q3) Look at the dimensions of the data.  There should be 26 samples.
```{r}
dim(data)
```

## Q4) Print the sample names to screen.
```{r}
colnames(data)
```

## Q5) Basic Scatter Plot across two patients
Plot the second SLE patient sample versus the first normal control samples in an xy scatter plot.  Remember that the first argument is the x vector.  Label the x and y-axes as 'Normal' and 'SLE', respectively.  Title the plot, 'SLE B cell sample vs. Normal B cell sample – all probesets'.  Add grey grid lines with the function grid(). 
```{r}
# Selecting Subsets of Data
normal1 <- data[, 1]   # first normal control sample
sle2    <- data[, 10]  # second SLE patient sample

# Scatter plot 
plot(normal1, sle2, 
          xlab = "Normal", ylab = "SLE", 
          main = "SLE B cell sample vs. Normal B cell sample – all probesets", 
          pch = 16, col = "black") 
        # Add grey grid lines 
        grid(col = "grey")
```

## Q6) Now do the same plot but pick only the first 20 probesets.  
Use the pch=15 argument to change the shape and color the points blue with the col argument.   
```{r}

# First normal control and second SLE sample
normal1 <- data[1:20, 1]   # first 20 rows of Normal sample
sle2    <- data[1:20, 10]  # first 20 rows of SLE sample

plot(normal1, sle2,
     xlab = "Normal",
     ylab = "SLE",
     main = "SLE B cell sample vs. Normal B cell sample – first 20 probesets",
     pch = 15,           # solid square
     col = "blue")       # color the points blue

grid(col = "grey")
```

## Q7) Now plot the following gene in a gene profile plot, IGLJ3 (immunoglobulin lambda joining 3)
which is probeset ID 211881_x_at.  This type of plot has the sample indices across the x-axis and the intensities on the y-axis, so you can see a profile of the gene across experiments or arrays.  First plot the ranges using the type=”n” argument and the plot() function, then add the genes with the lines() function call.  Add grid lines.
```{r}
# Extract the expression values for IGLJ3
gene_id <- "211881_x_at"
igl_values <- as.numeric(data[gene_id, ])

# X-axis = sample indices (1 through 26)
x_vals <- 1:ncol(data)

# Set up the plot ranges with type = "n" (draws axes but no points/lines yet)
plot(range(x_vals), 
     range(igl_values), 
     type = "n",
     xlab = "Sample Index",
     ylab = "Expression Intensity",
     main = paste("Gene Profile:", gene_id))

# Add the line plot for IGLJ3
lines(x_vals, igl_values, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

# Add grid lines
grid(col = "grey")

```

## Q8) Box Plot question
```{r}

## Q8 — Boxplot of IGLJ3 (211881_x_at) across SLE vs Control
## Rows = genes (probesets), cols = samples; SLE first (17), then Control (9)

gene_probe <- "211881_x_at"

# Expression vector for IGLJ3 across all 26 samples (columns)
y <- as.numeric(data[gene_probe, ])

# Condition factor: 17 SLE first, then 9 Control (and show SLE first on the x-axis)
f <- factor(c(rep("SLE", 17), rep("Control", 9)),
            levels = c("SLE", "Control"))

# Align lengths and drop any NAs
y <- y[seq_len(length(f))]
keep <- !is.na(y)
y <- y[keep]; f <- f[keep]

# Boxplot + optional stripchart overlay
boxplot(y ~ f,
        xlab = "Condition",
        ylab = "IGLJ3 Expression",
        main = "Q8: IGLJ3 (211881_x_at) — SLE vs Control")

with(data.frame(y, f),
     stripchart(y ~ f, method = "jitter", vertical = TRUE, pch = 16, add = TRUE))
```
